targetSpellingReason: TARGET SPELLING UPDATED 2026-10-11 for the same reason as the sibling fixtures: the CSS base qualifies targets with their stylesheet (`<file>::<name>`) and its own 51 expectation rows use that spelling. The containment, its line and `isMediaScope` are unchanged.
rationale: Two things this lane's other fixtures do not pin. (1) SCOPE CONTAINMENT: the CSS lane gets `contains` edges from `@media`/`@layer`/`@container`/`@scope` through its own at-rule handling, and the SCSS lane DELEGATES that walk — so `contains` works here, but nothing in this lane's fixtures asserted it, and a delegation is exactly the kind of thing that can stop being wired without any local test noticing. The nesting depth and the `:nth-child` are there to make the selector non-trivial rather than a bare class. (2) COMPLEXITY: the payload matrix needs a pin, and the CSS lane's complexity-matrix fixture is written in CSS — it cannot exercise a mixin's parameter count or an `@if`/`@else chain, which are the constructs that make SCSS complexity differ from CSS complexity at all. The `else if` arm is included because it is the form that a one-armed `@if` pin would miss. The first draft asserted `uses @if $steps > 4 -> @mixin ladder`, which is a relationship the file does not contain — the `@if` is INSIDE the mixin and nothing includes anything. Authoring an expectation and then failing against the analyzer is the fixture working: the alternative is a fixture transcribed from output, which cannot fail.
